title: Shrink the Number
statement: A lucky-number machine shrinks any whole number `n`: it adds up the digits, and if the result still has more than one digit, it does the same again, until one digit is left. Return that digit. Write it with recursion: the answer for `n` is the answer for the sum of its digits.

answerKey.pattern: Recursion with a base case of one digit
keyPoints: Base case: if n < 10, return n
Recursive case: compute the digit sum of n and return the answer for that smaller number
Each call works on a much smaller number, so the recursion ends quickly
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(d) per round for d digits; only a few rounds
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(number of rounds) for the call stack, a handful
edgeCases: A sum that needs several rounds
acceptableSlowerApproaches: A loop instead of recursion is equally fine
The 1 + (n - 1) % 9 formula is faster but skips the recursion this problem practises

hints: The stopping point is your base case: a number below 10 is its own answer.
Otherwise add the digits (n % 10, then n / 10 rounded down) and call the same function on the sum.
